brief.topic: A Score That Rewards Honest Uncertainty

s01: A forecast can be uncertain and still be the best forecast.
Suppose rain really has an eighty percent chance. We announce a probability.
The outcome is one for rain, zero for no rain.
Square the distance from our forecast to that outcome. Lower is better.
At eighty percent, rain gives an error of zero point zero four. No rain gives zero point six four.
Weight those two errors by their true chances.
The expected score is zero point one six.
Announcing certainty gives zero error in rain, but one when it stays dry. Its expected score is zero point two.
Here is the whole landscape of expected scores.
It equals zero point one six, plus the square of our distance from zero point eight.
That extra square cannot be negative. The minimum is the true probability.
Now suppose the true chance is one half.
The bottom moves to one half, not to certainty.
This binary Brier score rewards honest probabilities in expectation. One surprising outcome alone cannot judge a forecaster.

Weight those two errors by their true chances. The expected score is zero point one six. Announcing certainty gives zero error in rain, but one when it stays dry. Its expected score is zero point two.

Here is the whole landscape of expected scores. It equals zero point one six, plus the square of our distance from zero point eight. That extra square cannot be negative. The minimum is the true probability.
